A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same HopCast study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite substantial changes in layout.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on five dynamical systems, a synthetic attention-span demonstration, and ablations, including numerical results in Table 2 and Tables 4–8.

after.justification: v4 retains the original dynamical-system experiments, synthetic demonstration, and appendix ablation results.

M1.justification: The Predictor-Corrector architecture, context inputs, shuffled training triplets, masked attention, loss, memory sampling, and interval construction remain unchanged. Describing correction as pattern retrieval adds explanation rather than a component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five dynamical systems and heteroscedastic sine example, retaining the same prediction targets and noise levels. The noise-generation revision concerns the reported protocol within this coverage.

E2.justification: Expectation, Moment Matching, and Trajectory Sampling with Probabilistic Ensembles remain the evaluated comparators in Table 2 and the corresponding analyses. Appendix A retains their procedures.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B replace Gaussian noise inside the differential equations with measurement noise added after deterministic integration. This substantially revises the stated data-generating protocol across all five systems. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun; splits, sample counts, metrics, and listed model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: All seven appendix ablation topics are retained: encoder architecture, initial-condition context, memory size, embedding dimension, sequence length, shuffling, and ensemble size. Reordering the last three analyses does not add or remove evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run reporting, the random-seed statement in Table 4, and the same accompanying uncertainty values. No new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure appears.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Table 2 and Tables 4–8 are unchanged, as are the corresponding plotted findings. Table 2 still reports average CE of 0.046 for HopCast and 0.075 for Trajectory Sampling. The revised noise description does not establish new numerical outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal noise model changes from additive terms in the ODEs to a separate observation equation, s = s̃ + ε, in Section 3 and Appendix B. The deterministic dynamics, Hopfield equations, interval formulas, and baseline derivations remain intact. Changing embedding notation from k to d is not a theoretical change.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusions retain the predictor-agnostic correction framework, calibrated and sharper intervals without uncertainty propagation, and improved predictive accuracy. Attention Span was already introduced and claimed in v3.

C2.justification: v4 removes the concluding discussion of separate per-variable correction models, their asserted parameter efficiency relative to deep ensembles, and further scalability work. The forecasting-horizon, fixed-sampling-interval, and manual-tuning limitations remain, with the sampling restriction expressed more explicitly.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly specifies adaptive-step RK45 integration and extraction at fixed sampling intervals; Section 3 explicitly states that the Predictor is trained on the Integrated dataset. Appendix E retains the hardware, architectures, optimization settings, and supplementary YAML disclosure.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces environmental-health motivation and Currie et al. (2018) with cyber-physical-systems motivation citing Bilal Shahid and Fleming (2025), Shahid et al. (2024), and Robison et al. (2024). The main positioning against uncertainty-quantification and calibration research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized explanatory edits, standardizes embedding notation, uses Attention Span earlier, replaces the rainfall illustration with shorter sharpness motivation, and reorders Appendix D.5–D.7. The overall narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays undergo substantial redesign: v3 Figure 1 becomes v4 Figures 1–3, the sine demonstration and calibration comparison receive new panel arrangements, and the prediction-interval plot uses a shared legend. Figures, tables, and Algorithm 1 are extensively relocated and resized under a different page layout.

improvement.justification: v4 more clearly separates measurement noise from deterministic dynamics, documents numerical integration, and makes the dense method illustration easier to inspect through separate figures. These improve clarity and reproducibility without adding empirical evidence. The deleted scalability discussion and awkward float and page breaks partly offset these modest gains.
